# Linked sizes, in BYTES, of the self-host driver binaries CI already builds —
# checked against every run by scripts/ci-check-driver-sizes (#6826).
#
# WHICH BINARY IS "THE SELF-HOST BINARY": fern.fern, named below as the tracked
# artifact. It is examples/self_host/fern.fern, the whole self-hosted compiler
# CLI, and it is the number to quote when talking about self-host binary size
# (#4109's "well under half" target is against it). The others in this file are
# smaller programs that link a SUBSET of the compiler: `asm_ir_run` is the
# front-end plus the x86-64 IR backend, `wasm_ir_run` the front-end plus the
# wasm one, and so on. They are recorded because they are free to record and
# they localise a regression to a backend — NOT because they are
# interchangeable. Quoting one against another is how #4109 acquired a bogus
# "the epic is 4x off": a 245 MB CLI figure compared with a 59 MB wasm_ir_run
# figure.
#
# tracked-artifact: fern.fern
#
# HOW THIS IS MEASURED. Nothing extra is built. Every driver here is linked by
# the `warm` / `cli` jobs of test-e2e-selfhost.yml on their own account;
# TestSelfHostWarmStockDriver stats each one it warms into
# FERN_DRIVER_SIZE_REPORT, and the job compares that report against this file.
# The emit and the link are in-process pure Go, so a given commit yields the
# same byte count on any runner — a difference here is a real change in the
# compiler's output, not runner noise.
#
# ENFORCED, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Drift past FERN_SIZE_TOLERANCE_PERCENT (5% by
# default) is a job-summary line plus a warning annotation in whichever job
# linked the driver, and a FAILED `driver-sizes` job. That leaf compares the
# UNION of every measuring job's report and is the only place the fifteen are
# weighed as a set; the per-job checks stay advisory because their jobs gate the
# test shards, and a measurement step must not hold the lane. A SHRINK is
# flagged too: an un-updated baseline after a win silently raises the ceiling
# the next regression is measured against, which is how 16% of growth went
# unnoticed for eight days — and, in the other direction, how a 3.0 MB win was
# never recorded either (#7519).
#
# A DRIVER THAT WENT UNMEASURED FAILS TOO. `driver-sizes` sets
# FERN_SIZE_REPORT_COMPLETE=1, so a name in this file that reached no report is
# a finding instead of a row nobody notices is absent. Every measuring job links
# a disjoint set and used to check only that set, so a five-row table ending in
# "every driver is within 5% of its baseline" was indistinguishable from a
# fifteen-row one — which is how the drivers grew 2.3x with the gate green.
#
# WHEN A NUMBER MOVES ON PURPOSE, update it in the same PR — the job summary
# prints the corrected lines ready to paste. Keep the reason in the PR, not
# here; this file is a set of current facts.
#
# x86-64. The `warm` and `cli` jobs are x86-only (the aarch64 lane skips the x86
# driver builds), so there is one architecture to baseline and no per-arch split.
#
# REFRESHED after #6928 (.bss laid out last, so the ELF writer's zero-fill
# trim reaches it). TWO INDEPENDENT MOVEMENTS ARE FOLDED INTO THESE NUMBERS
# and they point opposite ways — do not read either figure as one effect:
#
#   1. The five drivers that link the strbuf runtime fell 78-84%, because
#      `__fern_strbuf_data`'s 64 MiB .bss reservation is no longer written to
#      the file. Measured on one host, same tree, fix in vs out: fern.fern
#      85,581,884 -> 18,473,012. That is the #6928 win and it is confined to
#      those five; for a driver without strbuf the output is BYTE-IDENTICAL
#      with and without the fix (verified on irlower_run).
#   2. Every driver also grew ~348 KB of .text against the previous baseline,
#      from self-host source changes that landed between the two refreshes.
#      That is why the ten non-strbuf drivers show +3.0% to +8.9% here: it is
#      main moving, not a codegen regression.
#
# Refreshed before that after #4111 (8-byte operand-stack slots + real
# push/pop on the x86-64 backend), which cut code density ~19% across the
# board.
#
# Refreshed before that after #6894 (exit-sweep drop outlining), which cut
# every driver: the tracked artifact by 42.5%, the front-end-only drivers by
# over 80%.
#
# THE PREVIOUS REFRESH'S FIGURES DID NOT REPRODUCE, and the first complete
# comparison is what caught it. #7677 recorded fifteen numbers that read 13-16%
# HIGH against what the same tree links: thirteen of them tripped the shrink
# check on the first `driver-sizes` run, uniformly, on a diff that touches no
# compiler code. Three things were established before these numbers replaced
# them, because a baseline nobody can reproduce is how this file failed before:
#
#   1. The method reproduces CI EXACTLY. checker_modload_run rebuilt off-CI at
#      the head CI measured gives 7,053,860 against CI's 7,053,860 — the
#      determinism this file asserts, demonstrated rather than trusted.
#   2. It also DISCRIMINATES, which an agreeing number alone does not show.
#      Walking that driver back over the commits that touch its import closure
#      moves it 7,033,212 -> 7,205,244, so the measurement follows the source.
#   3. The old figure is not a stale checkout. checker_modload_run's closure is
#      unchanged between #7677's own commit and this one, so its size cannot
#      have moved in that window, and 8,171,948 — what #7677 wrote for it —
#      occurs nowhere in the surrounding history.
#
# So the drivers did not shrink; the previous numbers were wrong when written.
# What produced them is NOT known, and that is the honest state: they are not
# this tree's output at that commit, at the commit before it, or at any commit
# sampled around it. #7519's attribution of the GROWTH before #7677 stands on
# its own evidence and is unaffected.
#
# Every figure below is CI's own, from the `driver-sizes` job's union of the
# `cli` and three `warm` reports on the head that recorded them — the first
# time all fifteen were compared in one place. The two the union did not print
# (ssa_run, ssa_emit_run, both inside tolerance and so not in its paste block)
# were linked off-CI with the method item 1 validates.
#
# Note the two tiers: the three drivers at 3.1-3.7 MB link a front-end slice
# only, while the rest sit at 12-19 MB. A small driver moving 5% is a different
# quantity of bytes from the tracked artifact moving 5%; the percentage is what
# is compared, deliberately, so a small driver's regression is not lost inside a
# big one's noise.
#
# WHAT THE FIFTEEN DO NOT SEE (#7519). These drivers are not a sample of the
# compiler. Each links one import closure, and a module outside it contributes
# nothing to that driver's bytes — so a change of any size registers at its full
# cost against some of these numbers and as exactly zero against others. Three
# consequences, before you quote a figure or add a driver:
#
#   * FOURTEEN MODULES ARE VISIBLE ONLY THROUGH fern.fern: both native back
#     ends (x86_native, arm64_native), elf, watbin, ssa_wasm, interp, printer,
#     constfold, literate, ferndoc, mvs, caps, platforms, visibility. A change
#     confined to one of them moves a single number in this file, and moves it
#     against the largest denominator here, where 300 KB is 0.8% and vanishes
#     under the tolerance. The claim above that the smaller drivers "localise a
#     regression to a backend" holds for the IR, asm and wasm-IR backends and
#     NOT for the native emitters, which have no localising driver at all.
#   * THREE LIBRARY MODULES ARE LINKED BY NO BASELINED DRIVER: wit_decode
#     (1,127 lines, imported nowhere in the tree), wit_compose, and
#     wasm_objfile — the last reachable only from wasm_modload_run, which
#     wasm-wholecompiler-link builds as a WASM module rather than an x86-64
#     ELF, a size that does not belong in this file's one architecture.
#     Covering it means paying for an x86-64 link of a driver nothing else
#     needs. Three neighbours look like they belong on this list and do not:
#     builtins.fern is never imported — modloader READS it at runtime
#     (`read_file(dir + "builtins.fern")`), so it is a source input rather
#     than linked code — while pipeline.fern and wasm_units_probe.fern carry
#     their own `main` and are unbaselined PROGRAMS, not unlinked modules.
#   * FIVE DRIVERS COVER TWO CLOSURES: asm_pathprobe_run and asm_ir_elig_run
#     have identical import closures, as do wasm_ir_run, wasm_run and
#     wasm_runio_run. They differ in what their `main` reaches, not in what
#     they link, so the three wasm rows are close to one measurement.
#
# PICK THE DENOMINATOR THAT SEES YOUR CHANGE. A change confined to one module is
# honestly measured against the SMALLEST driver linking it, not against the
# tracked artifact: checker.fern -> checker_modload_run (3.7 MB), the front end
# or ssa -> ssa_run (3.1 MB), irlower.fern -> asm_ir_elig_run (12.0 MB).
# Dividing by the wrong one is not a small error. #7519 found the 311-loop
# checker migration registering EXACTLY 0 bytes against irlower_run, which does
# not link checker.fern at all, and found one irlower slice reading +6.8% or
# +9.2% for the same absolute growth depending only on which driver divided it.

# WHY checker_modload_run MOVED +5.5% (7053860 -> 7438860). Crediting a
# match-arm binding as an owned projection source in rhsTainted's FieldAccess
# case (#7837) makes more locals free-eligible, and a free-eligible local's
# overwrite emits a deep drop where an ineligible one emitted the flat
# __fern_rc_dec that reclaims nothing. So the growth IS the reclaim code, paid
# once in .text against a leak that was unbounded in the heap: the examples
# corpus goes from 229,723 stranded allocations to 162,888, a 29% fall.
#
# It trips here and nowhere else because this is one of the three front-end
# slices, where 385 KB is 5.5% — the same bytes are 1.3% of the tracked
# artifact, which stayed inside tolerance. That is the two-tier point above
# working as intended rather than a checker-specific regression.

# WHY THE THREE FRONT-END SLICES SHRANK (-10.8%, -7.9%, -7.6%). Folding a
# uniqueness test on the null pointer. `OpRcIsUnique`'s own declaration says
# "sentinel/static -> 0" and every backend's helper opens with a null guard, so
# `is_unique(null)` is 0 — but `Fold` had no rule for the op, and
# `ConstPropagate` was already delivering a literal `const.i32 0` to 8456 of
# 15582 guards over the conformance corpus. Each one gated a deep drop of a
# slot holding the zero-init constant: an unreachable block of roughly 20 ops.
#
# Every one of the fifteen shrank, from -3.0% (the tracked artifact, 1 MB) to
# -10.8%. Only three breached tolerance, and they are the same front-end slices
# the note above records moving +5.5%: 385 KB is 5.5% of a 7 MB driver and 1.3%
# of a 30 MB one, which is the two-tier point working as intended again.
#
# It does NOT undo that growth. #7837 added deep drops that RUN, against an
# unbounded heap leak; this removes drop blocks that cannot. They are
# independent, and checker_modload_run now sits below its pre-#7837 figure
# (7053860) because the dead blocks predate both.

# 2026-08-31 — every row shrank 12–14.3%, and this is the whole table moving at
# once rather than a per-driver story: PruneZeroSlotGuards (#7787) deletes the
# scope-exit drop a frame emits for a local that was never assigned on the path
# reaching it, which is 10.9% of all IR ops over the self-host compiler. The
# tracked artifact fern.fern goes 30366508 -> 26733284, a 3.63 MB win. Numbers
# are the ones driver-sizes measured, pasted from its own corrected-baseline
# block — none is derived or scaled.

# 2026-09-01 — every row shrank 7.5–10.4%, the whole table again: the x86-64
# assembler now relaxes in-range jmp/jcc to their 2-byte rel8 forms (#7899),
# and every driver here is an x86-64 ELF it links. The tracked artifact goes
# 28080148 -> 25163796. Numbers pasted from driver-sizes' corrected-baseline
# block.

# 2026-09-01 — ten rows GREW 5.4%, two causes, measured apart on irlower_run:
# 18021740 (this table) -> 18279996 on plain main, +1.43% of drift nothing had
# banked, -> 19046076 with #6993's env-box lift on astwalk's accumulator spine,
# +4.19% more. The tracked artifact fern.fern goes 25163796 -> 26649772, +5.9%:
# it links every backend, so it pays the instantiation about twice over. It
# surfaced a run later than the rest only because the job reporting it is a
# different one — nothing about it was inside tolerance. The four small drivers
# (asm_ir_elig, checker_modload, ssa_run, ssa_emit) land at +1.2-1.5% and keep
# their numbers.
#
# The +4.19% is one monomorphised instantiation: map_expr_acc at InlineCloAcc
# is 2.1 MB of asm, map_stmt_acc 1.1 MB. The multiplier is the accumulator
# OWNING HEAP, not the walk being generic — the same fold_expr_nodes costs
# 28 KB at i32 and 353 KB at string, 13x for the type argument alone, and a
# rewriting spine reconstructs every node on top of that. Consumers added later
# at the SAME T are free; a new heap-owning T costs this again. So prefer a
# scalar or index-like accumulator when a pass can be written that way (#6993).
#
# Banked with the growth understood rather than after the fact, which is the
# thing #6826 was written to prevent. Behaviour is unchanged: the whole
# compiler emitted through the pre- and post-port compilers is byte-identical
# on x86-64 and wasm.

# 2026-09-02 — three rows grew past tolerance; the other twelve moved +0.5-4.6%
# and keep their numbers. One commit tips all three: 78045cb (ir: reclaim own
# accumulators through recursion and variant-payload temps). Bisected on
# checker_modload_run over the 86 commits since the previous refresh, then
# confirmed on the other two. Those deltas were measured with the in-process
# linker rather than CI's asm-plus-gcc path, so read them as deltas and not
# against the figures below:
#
#   checker_modload_run   3748748 -> 4019084   (+7.2%, and its whole breach)
#   asm_load_run         15943420 -> 16541436  (+3.8%, on +1.0% of prior drift)
#   fern.fern            19648332 -> 20250444  (+3.1%, on +3.4% of prior drift)
#
# The growth is reclaim code, as #7837's was: seeding findReturnsFreshBox with
# an `own` parameter keeps a threaded accumulator free-eligible, and crediting a
# variant-constructor payload store makes more locals emit a deep drop where a
# flat __fern_rc_dec stood. It buys the leaks that commit's census takes to zero
# — own-accumulator recursion 100-256 blocks, string-keyed ordmap insert 1637,
# pmap insert 500. checker_modload_run breaches on 78045cb alone; the other two
# were already carrying drift nothing had banked and cross the line with it.
#
# Numbers pasted from driver-sizes' corrected-baseline block.

fern.fern 14647852

asm_ir_run.fern 10671740
